definitions.gloss: rubber boots; rain boots; Wellington boots
definitions.explanation: Waterproof boots, typically made of rubber, worn in rainy weather, when working in muddy or wet conditions, or for outdoor activities. Also refers to tall boots in general.

examples.japanese: {雨|あめ}の{日|ひ}は{長靴|ながぐつ}を{履|は}く。
examples.english: I wear rain boots on rainy days.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもが{赤|あか}い{長靴|ながぐつ}で{水|みず}たまりに{入|はい}って{遊|あそ}んでいる。
examples.english: The child is playing in puddles wearing red rain boots.

examples.japanese: {畑仕事|はたけしごと}をするときは、いつも{長靴|ながぐつ}を{履|は}いている。
examples.english: When doing farm work, I always wear rubber boots.

notes:
USAGE:
In everyday Japanese, {長靴|ながぐつ} most commonly refers to rubber rain boots. Children's rain boots in bright colors are especially associated with this word. For fashionable tall boots, ブーツ or ロングブーツ are more commonly used.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {長靴|ながぐつ}を{履|は}く (put on / wear rain boots)
- ゴム{長靴|ながぐつ} (rubber boots — emphasizing the material)
- {子|こ}ども{用|よう}の{長靴|ながぐつ} (children's rain boots)

CULTURAL NOTE:
{長靴|ながぐつ}をはいた{猫|ねこ} (Puss in Boots) is the standard Japanese title for the famous fairy tale.
